answer: Edge-History Accrual requires each new identity to inherit a routing-history deficit: it starts off the sparse ocean of verified relay paths and must accumulate distinct, timestamped forwarding records from existing agents before gaining full broadcast weight. Each record is only issued along an already-trusted path, so a cluster of new nodes on one knoll of the graph cannot mutually certify. An attacker must sustain real traffic and latency across many genuine regions, paying bandwidth and time per identity, with growth capped at one juniper-thin edge per epoch.
